issues.title: Reuse hash values during Aggregate(partial) -> Repartition -> Aggregate(final)
issues.body:
Still in draft 🙈, expect heavy changes

## Which issue does this PR close?

<!--
We generally require a GitHub issue to be filed for all bug fixes and enhancements and this helps us generate change logs for our releases. You can link an issue to this PR using the GitHub syntax. For example `Closes #123` indicates that this PR will close issue #123.
-->

- Closes #11680.

## Rationale for this change

<!--
 Why are you proposing this change? If this is already explained clearly in the issue then this section is not needed.
 Explaining clearly why changes are proposed helps reviewers understand your changes and offer better suggestions for fixes.  
-->

During partial + final aggregations, in order to accumulate + repartition data cross partitions, a hash is computed over the grouping expressions.

This hash is computed 3 times:

```rust
Aggregate(final): 3rd time hash computed 
  Repartition: 2nd time hash computed
    Aggregate(partial): 1st time hash computed
```

And depending on what's getting hashed, it can be an expensive operation (e.g., hashing arbitrary length strings).

This PR introduces a mechanism that allows reusing the hashes across different operators, by propagating them under an internal column in the schema:

```rust
Aggregate(final): precomputed 
  Repartition: precomputed
    Aggregate(partial): 1st time hash computed
```

## What changes are included in this PR?

<!--
There is no need to duplicate the description in the issue here but it is sometimes worth providing a summary of the individual changes in this PR.
-->

Introduces to core structs that aim to set the foundations of hash reuse across operators:
- `ExpressionHasher`: handles hashing columns based on expressions, maintaining an internal buffer for reusing allocations, stamping the hashes into internal columns so that they can cross operator boundaries, and retrieving those hashes from the internal columns if present.
- `GroupHashTracker`: during groupings, it keeps track of the per-group hashes so that operators that aggregate can emit them as an additional internal column for reuse purposes.

These two structs are used across all the aggregation implementations in the codebase for reusing hashes.

Additionally, some metrics for tracking how many hashes where computed VS how many hashes where reused are also added to operators that need to deal with hashes

## Are these changes tested?

<!--
We typically require tests for all PRs in order to:
1. Prevent the code from being accidentally broken by subsequent changes
2. Serve as another way to document the expected behavior of the code

If tests are not included in your PR, please explain why (for example, are they covered by existing tests)?
-->

Yes, by existing and new tests.

## Are there any user-facing changes?

<!--
If there are user-facing changes then we may require documentation to be updated before approving the PR.
-->

<!--
If there are any breaking changes to public APIs, please add the `api change` label.
-->

No, this should be transparent to users.

issues.title: [final state] optional filters stack (do not merge)
issues.body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

- Part of https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/22883. Design notes: https://claude.ai/artifact/SSz7t6hPyhFWp1MDPecVqt
- **Do not merge.** This is the "final state" of the optional filters stack: all pieces, in one linear history on `main`, for benchmarks and for a review of the complete design. Review the code in the PR of each piece (table below).
- Alternative API design (prototype): https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25760.

## Rationale for this change

With `pushdown_filters = true`, the Parquet scan evaluates each pushed filter row by row. Some filters make the query slower than with pushdown off:

| Case | Why it is slow |
|---|---|
| A dynamic filter (hash join, TopK, aggregate) that removes few rows | the scan pays the evaluation for every row, the join or the TopK checks the rows again |
| A filter that costs more than the work that it saves downstream | for example a hash lookup of 12 ns for each row in front of a join probe of 2 to 8 ns |
| A filter in the Parquet `RowFilter` that removes rows in a scattered pattern | a row filter stage costs 4 to 16 ns for each row, and the decoder still decodes all pages |
| A filter on a small scan that `FilterPushdown` removes from the plan | the optimizer then adds no round-robin repartition, and the filter runs in one partition |

This is a main reason why `pushdown_filters` is off by default (https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/20324). The stack makes the scan decide, from measurements, where to evaluate each filter and whether to evaluate an optional filter at all.

## What changes are included in this PR?

Linear history on current `main` (fb88eb529b), 60 commits: the current head of each PR in the table, and two integration commits (the tests of #25729 and #25727 show `Optional(DynamicFilter [...])` with #25681; the `parquet_statistics.slt` case of https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25795 has no `FilterExec` with #22384). This branch and https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25715 are the same commit. Each change is here one time. The shared `filter_stats` commit and the `PRE_SELECTION_THRESHOLD` change of #25721 and #25727 are here one time. The defaults commits (#25715) are the last three commits.

### PR map

| PR | Content | State |
|---|---|---|
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25729 | Page index: no row selection when it prunes nothing | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25677 | Hash join: collapse partitioned `InList` dynamic filters into one IN list | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25713 | Hash join: push bounds and membership as separate filters | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/22384 | Parquet: accept all pushable filters, run rejected conjuncts post-scan; keep a filter above a scan that cannot give the target partitions (R4) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25673 | `OptionalFilterPhysicalExpr` (A1) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25722 | Post-scan filter keeps optional filters pruning-only | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25721 | `filter_stats` and `FilterExec` adaptive conjunct reordering (B2) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25674 | `OptionalFilterGate`, shared pauses, `RemovedRowWork` (A3) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25682 | `optional_filter_mode` config and Parquet consumer (A4) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25683 | `FilterExec` gates optional filters (B1) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25681 | Producers mark hash join, TopK and aggregate dynamic filters as optional; the hash join measures its probe work (A2) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25727 | Adaptive placement of scan filter conjuncts (E3) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25715 | Defaults: `optional_filter_mode = adaptive` and `adaptive_filter_placement = true` (A5) | Open, draft |
| https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25726 | Per-conjunct pruning statistics (E2) | Closed: the placement has no statistics prior any more. Not in this branch |

```mermaid
graph LR
  PI["#25729 page index select-all"]
  C1["#25677 InList collapse"]
  C2["#25713 split join filter"]
  P["#22384 post-scan filter + R4"]
  A1["#25673 Optional wrapper"]
  F["#25722 post-scan skips optional"]
  B2["#25721 filter_stats + reordering"]
  A3["#25674 gate"]
  A4["#25682 mode + Parquet consumer"]
  B1["#25683 FilterExec consumer"]
  A2["#25681 producers + probe work"]
  E3["#25727 adaptive placement"]
  A5["#25715 adaptive defaults"]
  C1 --> C2 --> A2
  A1 --> A2
  A3 --> A2
  P --> F
  A1 --> F
  B2 -. shares filter_stats .- A3
  A3 --> A4
  A1 --> A4
  A3 --> B1
  A1 --> B1
  B2 --> B1
  A4 --> E3
  F --> E3
  PI --> E3
  E3 --> A5
  B1 --> A5
  A2 --> A5
```

### Design

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Producers
    HJ[HashJoinExec]
    TK[TopK]
    AG[AggregateExec]
  end
  HJ -- "Optional(DynamicFilter) + RemovedRowWork" --> SCAN
  TK -- "Optional(DynamicFilter)" --> SCAN
  AG -- "Optional(DynamicFilter)" --> SCAN
  subgraph SCAN[Parquet scan]
    PL{placement per conjunct} --> RF[RowFilter]
    PL --> PS[post-scan filter]
    PL --> SK[Skip: gate paused]
  end
  HJ -- "Optional(...)" --> FE[FilterExec: gate per optional conjunct]
```

| Part | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Optional filters (A1, A2) | `Optional(expr)` marks a conjunct that is not needed for correctness. Hash join, TopK and aggregate dynamic filters are optional. A consumer can skip an optional conjunct; statistics pruning always uses it |
| Gate (A3) | One `OptionalFilterGate` per stream and optional conjunct. At the end of each window (at least 2 batches and `MIN_OBSERVED_ROWS` rows) it pauses the filter when `cost > rows_removed × saving` (1.1 to pause, 0.9 to resume). A pause doubles on each confirmation (4 to 32 batches); a probe window follows each pause; a change of the dynamic filter starts again |
| Gate cost | measured evaluation time + `rows_in × overhead`, where the overhead is the measured stage cost of the consumer (8 ns for each row for a Parquet row filter stage, 0 in the post-scan filter and in `FilterExec`) |
| Gate saving | the work that the producer measures for each removed row (`RemovedRowWork`: the hash join records the evaluation, the hashes and the lookup of probe rows without a match) + the saving that the consumer measures (Parquet: decode time of the unread output columns for the skippable rows). Before the producer has `MIN_OBSERVED_ROWS` rows, and for producers that do not measure (TopK, aggregate), the saving is the tunable estimate `optional_filter_min_saving_ns_per_row` (20 ns) |
| Shared pauses | The gates of one optional filter in all files and partitions of a scan share their pauses (`SharedGateVerdict`, one atomic word). A new gate starts paused; a gate that keeps the filter ignores the pauses of the others |
| Placement (E3) | For each conjunct, required or optional, at file open and at each row group boundary: `PostScan`, `RowFilter` or `Skip` (optional, gate paused). A conjunct starts `PostScan` and moves to `RowFilter` only on measured evidence: benefit (skippable rows × unread output bytes × decode ns/byte + measured post-scan copy) against cost (8 ns stage cost + fetch latency + second decode of the read output columns). Margins 0.9 / 1.1 and hysteresis on changes. No statistics prior |
| Order | In each stage, by measured rows removed for each nanosecond; unmeasured conjuncts first, so that they are measured on all rows. The `RowFilter` order changes at row group boundaries, the post-scan order at each batch |
| Post-scan filter (#22384) | The scan accepts all pushable filters. Conjuncts that are not in the `RowFilter` run on the decoded batches in the scan. The working batch is compacted only when a conjunct keeps at most 20% of the rows (the pre-selection threshold of `AND`) |
| R4 (#22384) | When a scan has fewer partitions than `target_partitions`, cannot be split further, and a round-robin repartition is useful, the filters of a `FilterExec` stay above the scan (as on `main`), so the optimizer keeps the parallel plan. The scan still gets them as a pruning-only predicate (`FileSource::try_pushdown_pruning_filters`, proto `pruning_only_predicate`) and uses them only to prune files, row groups and pages. A scan with a pruning-only predicate uses later filters only to prune too |
| Scan equivalences (https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25780 on `main`) | The scan derives equivalences only from the conjuncts that it applies to every row (`FileSource::exact_filter`): the accepted conjuncts, also with `pushdown_filters = false` (post-scan filter). A pruning-only predicate (R4) and optional conjuncts (the gate or the placement can skip them) are never exact |
| `FilterExec` (B1, B2) | Required conjuncts can be reordered by measured cost (`adaptive_filter_reordering`, off by default). Optional conjuncts run behind a gate after them |

### Remaining constants

| Constant | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| `filter_stats::MIN_OBSERVED_ROWS` | 8192 rows | One default batch. With fewer rows, the fixed cost of each call dominates the evaluation time (ClickBench Q23: 600 to 8000 ns for each row on batches of 2 to 7 rows, against 0.4 ns on full batches) |
| Gate window and backoff (`sample_batches`, `initial_pause_batches`, `max_pause_batches`) | 2, 4, 32 batches | A window needs more than one batch; the pause doubles so that a filter that stays useless costs `O(log)` probes. Fields of `OptionalFilterGateConfig` |
| Gate margins | 1.1 to pause, 0.9 to resume | Prevent flapping near the break-even point |
| `optional_filter_min_saving_ns_per_row` | 20 ns | A prior only: used until the producer has a measurement, and for producers that do not measure. A hash table probe measured about 13 ns. Tunable config |
| `ROW_FILTER_STAGE_NS_PER_ROW` | 8 ns | Profiles of TPC-H SF1 Q6, Q12 and Q4: 4 to 16 ns for each row and stage, independent of the predicate |
| `SKIP_WINDOW_ROWS` | 64 rows | The decoder skips only runs of removed rows (its `RowSelectionPolicy::Auto` threshold is 32); one `u64` of the filter result |
| `DEFAULT_DECODE_NS_PER_BYTE` | 4 ns | A prior until the scan measures its decode speed (TPC-DS SF1: 4 to 8 ns for each compressed byte) |
| Placement margins | 0.9 to enter the row filter, 1.1 to leave it | The same margins as the gate |
| Placement hysteresis | 2^(n-1) - 1 row group boundaries after the n-th change | At most log2(row groups) + 1 decoder rebuilds for each file (ClickBench Q25 had 128) |
| Post-scan compaction threshold | 0.2 (`PRE_SELECTION_THRESHOLD`) | The threshold of `AND` in `BinaryExpr`, thus the same copy decision as the `FilterExec` that the post-scan filter replaces. TPC-DS Q82 and TPC-H Q14, Q15, Q12 are faster with it; 0 (never compact) is slower on TPC-H Q20 and TPC-DS Q42, Q52, Q55 |
| `FilterExec` reordering (`WARMUP_BATCHES`, `MIN_GAIN`) | 8 batches, 5% | #25721, off by default |

## What is the testing strategy for this PR?

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p datafusion-physical-expr -p datafusion-physical-plan --lib` | Pass |
| `cargo test -p datafusion-datasource-parquet` | Pass |
| `cargo test -p datafusion-proto` | Pass |
| `cargo test -p datafusion --test parquet_integration --test core_integration` | Pass |
| `cargo test --test sqllogictests` | Pass |
| `ci/scripts/rust_clippy.sh`, `ci/scripts/rust_docs.sh` | Pass |

Also `ci/scripts/rust_clippy.sh`, `ci/scripts/rust_docs.sh` and `ci/scripts/doc_prettier_check.sh` pass on this branch. Each piece PR has its own tests.

### Benchmark bot results (head f1036e8f37)

Min-time table, ratio = branch / `main`. `main` = the merge-base fb88eb529b with `pushdown_filters = false`. Branch = `pushdown_filters = true`, adaptive defaults. Two runs: https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25752#issuecomment-5864886638 and https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25752#issuecomment-5864886861.

| Suite | Run 1 | Run 2 | `pruning_only` mode (a85abe2) | A/A spread (largest \|ratio - 1\|) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TPC-H SF1 | 0.900 | 0.911 | 1.005 | 2.2% |
| TPC-DS SF1 | 0.761 | 0.771 | 0.994 | 5.6% |
| ClickBench partitioned | 0.828 | 0.828 | 0.842 | 6.9% |

The A/A control (https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25752#issuecomment-5839971302) ran `main` against itself: no query is more than 7% off. A "real" regression is more than 7% slower in both runs and above the A/A spread.

The totals are the same as for the previous head 8a66fd060a within noise. The small increase on TPC-H and TPC-DS comes from `main`: between the two heads, `main` got 3 to 7% faster (median query time), and the branch 1 to 4%. For example TPC-DS Q11 went from 0.85 / 0.90 to 0.99 / 0.99: the branch time did not change (263 ms against 267 ms), `main` went from 315 ms to 266 ms. TPC-DS Q23, Q14, Q4 and TPC-H Q21 lost part of their win in the same way.

Biggest wins (both runs):

| Query | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| TPC-DS Q72 | 0.05 | 0.06 |
| ClickBench Q23 | 0.06 | 0.07 |
| TPC-DS Q8 | 0.37 | 0.39 |
| TPC-DS Q15 | 0.43 | 0.44 |
| TPC-DS Q54 | 0.53 | 0.55 |
| TPC-DS Q2 | 0.56 | 0.55 |
| TPC-H Q17 | 0.60 | 0.60 |
| TPC-H Q18 | 0.66 | 0.65 |

Remaining regressions (adaptive mode, beyond the A/A spread):

| Query | Run 1 | Run 2 | `pruning_only` mode | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TPC-DS Q52 | 1.13 | 1.10 | 1.01 | real |
| TPC-DS Q55 | 1.12 | 1.11 | 1.02 | real |
| TPC-DS Q31 | 1.12 | 1.10 | 1.00 | real |
| TPC-DS Q69 | 1.08 | 1.11 | 1.02 | real |
| TPC-DS Q33 | 1.09 | 1.10 | 1.01 | real |
| TPC-DS Q42 | 1.10 | 1.10 | 1.02 | real |
| TPC-DS Q71 | 1.09 | 1.09 | 1.00 | real |
| TPC-H Q9 | 1.09 | 1.13 | 1.01 | real (branch time unchanged, `main` faster) |
| TPC-DS Q46 | 1.08 | 1.09 | 1.08 | borderline |
| TPC-DS Q60 | 1.08 | 1.07 | 1.01 | borderline |

TPC-DS Q92, Q34 and Q77 (borderline at 8a66fd060a) are now below 1.07. In `pruning_only` mode (optional filters only prune) the real regressions are at about 1.00 to 1.02. Thus their cost is the evaluation of optional filters that the gate keeps because its saving is an estimate: the configured `optional_filter_min_saving_ns_per_row`, not a measurement of the downstream work (follow-up issue: https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/25778). TPC-DS Q46 is also 1.08 in `pruning_only` mode, thus it does not come from this cost.

## Known limits and follow-ups

| Topic | State |
|---|---|
| Measurement of the downstream saving | Only the hash join measures the work that a removed row saves. TopK and aggregate filters, and joins before their first `MIN_OBSERVED_ROWS` probe rows, use the estimate `optional_filter_min_saving_ns_per_row`. Follow-up issue: https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/25778 |
| `HashJoinExec` eager build collection | The hash join collects its build side eagerly. Follow-up |
| Filter API | The optional marker is an expression wrapper (`Optional(...)`). The alternative is a physical filter API with optional conjuncts: https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/25760 (prototype) |

## Are there any user-facing changes?

Yes, from the pieces: new config options `optional_filter_mode`, `optional_filter_min_saving_ns_per_row`, `adaptive_filter_reordering` and `adaptive_filter_placement`, new scan and `FilterExec` metrics, and `Optional(...)` in plans. A5 changes two defaults (upgrade guide note in `56.0.0.md`). With R4, a small scan keeps its `FilterExec` above it, as on `main`.

issues.title: Supporting writing schema metadata when writing Parquet in parallel
issues.body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

Closes https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/11770

## Rationale for this change

The [ArrowWriter](https://docs.rs/parquet/53.3.0/parquet/arrow/arrow_writer/struct.ArrowWriter.html) with it's default `ArrowWriterOptions` will encode the arrow schema in the parquet kv_metadata, unless explicitly skipped. Skipping is done via [ArrowWriterOptions::with_skip_arrow_metadata](https://docs.rs/parquet/53.3.0/parquet/arrow/arrow_writer/struct.ArrowWriterOptions.html#method.with_skip_arrow_metadata).

In datafusion's ParquetSink, we can write in either single threaded or parallelized format. When in single-threaded mode, we use the default `ArrowWriterOptions` and the arrow schema is inserted into file kv_meta. However, when performing parallelized writes we do not use the ArrowWriter and instead rely upon the [SerializedFileWriter](https://docs.rs/parquet/53.3.0/parquet/file/writer/struct.SerializedFileWriter.html). As a result, we are missing the arrow schema metadata in the parquet files (see the issue ticket).

### ArrowWriterOptions vs WriterProperties

The SerializedFileWriter, along with other associated writers, rely upon the [WriterProperties](https://docs.rs/parquet/53.3.0/parquet/file/properties/struct.WriterProperties.html). The `WriterProperties` differ from the `ArrowWriterOptions` only in terms of the `skip_arrow_metadata` and the `schema_root`:

```
pub struct ArrowWriterOptions {
    properties: WriterProperties,
    skip_arrow_metadata: bool,
    schema_root: Option<String>,
}
```

The skip_arrow_metadata config is [only used to decide if the schema should be added](https://github.com/apache/arrow-rs/blob/2905ce6796cad396241fc50164970dbf1237440a/parquet/src/arrow/arrow_writer/mod.rs#L188-L190) to the `WriterProperties.kv_metadata`.

### Proposed Solution

Since we have WriterProperties, not ArrowWriterOptions, I focused on solutions which construct the proper `WriterProperties.kv_metadata` (with or without the arrow schema).

Our established pattern is to take `TableParquetOptions` configurations, and derive WriterProperties from those. Therefore, I updates those conversion methods to consider arrow schema insertion.

## What changes are included in this PR?

* add a new configuration `ParquetOptions.skip_arrow_metadata`
* have ParquetSink single-threaded writes, which use the ArrowWriter, respect this configuration
* have ParquetSink multiple-threaded writes, which use WriterProperties, respect this configuration
* `TableParquetOptions` => into `WriterProperties` conversion methods are updated 


## Are these changes tested?

yes.

## Are there any user-facing changes?

We have new APIs:
* `ParquetOptions.skip_arrow_metadata` configuration
* replace/deprecate `ParquetWriterOptions::try_from(ParquetWriterOptions)` and replace with methods which explicitly handle arrow schema

## Which issue does this PR close?

<!--
We generally require a GitHub issue to be filed for all bug fixes and enhancements and this helps us generate change logs for our releases. You can link an issue to this PR using the GitHub syntax. For example `Closes #123` indicates that this PR will close issue #123.
-->


Closes https://github.com/apache/arrow-datafusion/issues/6916

## Rationale for this change
We should have some more optimal defaults.

# Which issue does this PR close?

<!--
We generally require a GitHub issue to be filed for all bug fixes and enhancements and this helps us generate change logs for our releases. You can link an issue to this PR using the GitHub syntax. For example `Closes #123` indicates that this PR will close issue #123.

Closes #5879

# Rationale for this change

<!--
 Why are you proposing this change? If this is already explained clearly in the issue then this section is not needed.
 Explaining clearly why changes are proposed helps reviewers understand your changes and offer better suggestions for fixes.  
-->

Investigating https://github.com/apache/arrow-datafusion/pull/5292 and thought I would try to break it into smaller pieces to make it easier to see what is going on. In particular this PR just switches `ExternalSorter` to using `SortPreservingMerge`.

This results in better performance, apart from in the case of a single sort column. This is not hugely surprising, as lexsort_to_indices has optimised kernels for when sorting by a single column.
